title: Burst fairness and prefetch degeneracy patch to address tenant saturation escalations
creator: Priya Menon
description: High-severity customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments traced to a compound edge case: aggressive prefetch and KV cache warmup behavior combined with tenant-level request bursts causes eviction thrashing and long-context tail latency. The patch introduces a lightweight 'burst fairness shim' and a prefetch degeneracy detector to quarantine aggressive prefetch flows, apply a soft dequeue grace period for latency-sensitive short requests, and emit richer telemetry for autoscaler/ingress decisions.
reproduction_steps: 1) Recreate mixed-length synthetic workload: 75% short (<=64 tokens), 25% long (>=2048 tokens) against Dedicated pool with autoscaler enabled
2) Enable continuous prefetch and KV warmup flags (runtime.feature.prefetch=true runtime.kv.warmup=true)
3) Fire tenant-scoped microburst (200 concurrent short requests over 10s) while a long-context request batch is in-flight
4) Observe queue backlog growth, KV eviction rate spike, and short-request p95/p99 latency climbing 4x
5) Confirm same pattern on Private (upgrade window) and Hosted (multi-tenant shared pool) under identical workload profiles
investigation_notes: Telemetry shows correlated KV cache churn and admission window expansion during microbursts; eviction rate increases when prefetch pipeline is active
Root cause: prefetch degeneracy — warmup attempts for long requests aggressively touch KV space, causing eviction of hot prefixes used by short requests, amplifying queue wait times
Scheduler admission currently prioritizes efficient batch size and throughput; no short-request safeguard exists when prefetch/warmup is active
Private upgrade agent induced ephemeral topology changes exacerbate the timing window where prefetch and admission align badly
Customer escalations: AcmeHealth (Dedicated) and StreamlineDocs (Hosted) reported production regressions during nightly processing and tenant traffic spikes
proposed_fix: Introduce a minimal burst-fairness shim in the admission controller that: 1) detects tenant burst patterns and tags flow as 'burst-temporary', 2) applies a soft dequeue grace window that preferentially dequeues latency-sensitive short requests for the next N seconds, 3) installs a prefetch degeneracy detector which reduces prefetch aggressiveness when KV eviction rate or short-request latency crosses thresholds. Add telemetry hooks and feature flags for controlled rollouts.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in runtime-sim harness (branch: fix/burst-fairness-prefetch-61234)
2) Canary on Hosted small pool (10 nodes) with feature flag gated rollout for 48h
3) Apply to Dedicated as opt-in via console to high-severity customers for validation
4) Gradual Private release as part of private-2026.03 patch with upgrade-agent guardrails
5) Monitor p95/p99 short-request latency, KV eviction rate, and admission queue depth; rollback if regression >15%
